title: Conditional mutual information depends only on the joint law
statement: Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ and $(\Omega',\mu')$ be finite probability spaces, and let $S$, $T$, $U$ be finite sets. Consider random variables $X\colon\Omega\to S$, $Y\colon\Omega\to T$, $Z\colon\Omega\to U$ defined on the first space and $X'\colon\Omega'\to S$, $Y'\colon\Omega'\to T$, $Z'\colon\Omega'\to U$ defined on the second. If the joint random vectors $(X,Y,Z)$ and $(X',Y',Z')$ are identically distributed — that is, they induce the same probability measure on $S\times T\times U$ — then their conditional mutual informations agree: \[ I(X;Y\mid Z) = I(X';Y'\mid Z'). \]
hypotheses_covered: Ω and Ω' are finite (discrete) measurable spaces
S, T, U are finite value sets
μ and μ' are probability measures
X, Y, Z on Ω and X', Y', Z' on Ω' take values in S, T, U
(X,Y,Z) and (X',Y',Z') are identically distributed (same joint law)
